layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The DINO family of self-supervised vision models has shown remarkable trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferability, yet effectively adapting their representations for segmentation remains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging. Existing approaches often rely on heavy decoders with multi-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion or complex upsampling, which introduce substantial parameter overhead

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and computational cost. In this work, we propose SegDINO, an efficient seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation framework that couples a frozen DINOv3 backbone with a lightweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder. SegDINO extracts multi-level features from the pretrained encoder,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aligns them to a common resolution and channel width, and utilizes a lightweight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MLP head to directly predict segmentation masks. This design minimizes train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: able parameters while preserving the representational power of foundation fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures. Extensive experiments across six benchmarks, including three medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets (TN3K, Kvasir-SEG, ISIC) and three natural image datasets (MSD,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: VMD-D, ViSha), demonstrate that SegDINO consistently achieves state-of-the-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: art performance compared to existing methods. Code is available at https :

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: //github.com/script-Yang/SegDINO.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Image segmentation plays a central role in image analysis, serving as the foundation for down-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stream tasks such as object recognition (Minaee et al., 2021), scene understanding (Jain et al., 2023;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wang et al., 2024b), and computer-aided diagnosis (Azad et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024a; 2025a).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite remarkable progress achieved by convolutional networks (Long et al., 2015; Ronneberger

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2015), transformer-based models (Strudel et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024), diffusion-based archi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tectures (Amit et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2024), and Mamba-based frameworks (Ma et al., 2024; Xing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2024), these approaches often struggle to achieve strong generalization when training data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are limited (Zhang et al., 2021). Recent SAM-based segmentation models (Kirillov et al., 2023;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mazurowski et al., 2023) offer powerful zero-shot capabilities but typically require extensive fine-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuning for downstream tasks, leading to inefficiency (Zhang et al., 2024). Moreover, even in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frozen setting, the computational overhead of SAM models is substantial, making them less suitable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for lightweight or resource-constrained applications (Zhao et al., 2023). Consequently, the design

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of high-performance yet efficient segmentation frameworks remains an open challenge.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With the emergence of self-supervised foundation models (Caron et al., 2021; He et al., 2022),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretrained vision backbones have become increasingly prevalent for dense prediction. Rather than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training encoders from scratch, recent segmentation methods leverage large-scale pretrained repre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sentations to capture rich semantics and structural priors (Zhou et al., 2024b). In contrast to SAM-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based models, self-supervised vision models achieve a favorable balance by maintaining relatively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modest parameter counts while extracting high-quality semantic features (Siméoni et al., 2025),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: making them especially appealing for segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Among various self-supervised foundation models, the DINO family has demonstrated excep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional transferability across a wide range of visual tasks (Wang et al., 2025c; Gao et al., 2025).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DINO (Caron et al., 2021) and DINOv2 (Oquab et al., 2023) have been widely adopted for rep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resentation learning (Zhu et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025b), providing robust multi-scale features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suitable for detection (Damm et al., 2025) and segmentation (Ayzenberg et al., 2024). Most re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cently, DINOv3 (Siméoni et al., 2025) introduced significant improvements in pretraining strategies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and architectural refinements, achieving stronger invariance and scalability, and establishing itself

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a state-of-the-art pretrained backbone.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, effectively adapting DINO-based representations for segmentation tasks still remains a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-trivial challenge. Existing methods often employ relatively heavy decoders, such as multi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale fusion modules (Gao et al., 2025) or complex upsampling pipelines (Yang et al., 2025), which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduce substantial parameter overhead and computational cost. Such decoder complexity con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sequently offsets the efficiency advantages of frozen pretrained encoders and poses obstacles to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deployment in resource-constrained settings (Xie et al., 2021).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To address these limitations, we propose SegDINO, a segmentation framework that couples a frozen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DINOv3 backbone with a lightweight decoder. SegDINO leverages the DINO backbone to extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantically rich features and employs a light MLP-based head to directly predict segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks. This design minimizes the trainable parameter burden while preserving representational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: power from the foundation encoder. Extensive experiments on both medical and natural image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that SegDINO achieves competitive or superior accuracy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared to baselines while offering significant efficiency advantages.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 METHODOLOGY

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 OVERVIEW

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As illustrated in Fig. 2, an input image is fed to a pretrained, frozen DINOv3 model to extract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-layer features. The selected features are lightly upsampled to a common spatial resolution,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concatenated along the channel dimension, and passed to a lightweight decoder to produce the final

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation mask. During training, only the decoder is updated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 EXPERIMENTS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 DATASETS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Medical Image Datasets. We evaluate our method on three medical image segmentation bench-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marks. TN3K (Gong et al., 2023) is a large-scale thyroid nodule segmentation dataset, containing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3,493 ultrasound images with pixel-level annotations collected from multiple hospitals. Kvasir-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SEG (Jha et al., 2019) is a polyp segmentation dataset derived from colonoscopy examinations,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consisting of 1,000 images with high-quality expert annotations. ISIC (Codella et al., 2018) is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a skin lesion segmentation benchmark, providing 2,750 dermoscopic images annotated for lesion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundaries and covering a wide range of lesion types and acquisition conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Natural Image Datasets. We conduct experiments on three representative benchmarks covering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both mirror and shadow segmentation tasks. MSD (Yang et al., 2019) is a static image-based mir-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ror segmentation dataset, containing 4,018 annotated images from diverse scenarios such as indoor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mirrors, shop windows, and vehicle mirrors. VMD-D (Lin et al., 2023) is the first large-scale video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mirror detection dataset, which consists of 269 videos (14,988 frames) with high-resolution annota-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, capturing challenging dynamic conditions including camera motion, illumination variations,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and multiple mirrors. VISHA (Chen et al., 2021c) is a widely used benchmark for video shadow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection, providing 11,685 video frames with fine-grained annotations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Experimental Settings. For each dataset, we follow the official training-testing split provided by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the organizers to ensure fair comparison. All images are resized to 256 × 256 for consistent input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution across models, and normalized using the same mean and standard deviation parameters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as in DINOv3 (Siméoni et al., 2025).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We implement all experiments with the PyTorch framework (Paszke et al., 2019). The models are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimized using AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) with a learning rate of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a weight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decay of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . Cross-entropy loss is employed as the training objective. Training is conducted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for 50 epochs with a batch size of 4. For SegDINO, the DINO backbone is frozen, and only the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder parameters are updated. In this work, we exclusively adopt the DINOv3-S backbone, from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which intermediate features of the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th Transformer layers are extracted. All

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experiments are run on a cloud platform equipped with four NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Evaluation Metrics. For medical image datasets, we employ Dice similarity coefficient (DSC)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and IoU to measure overlap between predictions and ground truth, together with the 95th per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centile Hausdorff Distance (HD95) to evaluate boundary localization accuracy. For natural image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets, we adopt intersection over union (IoU), pixel accuracy (Accuracy), F-measure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Lin

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2023), mean absolute error (MAE), and balanced error rate (BER) to evaluate our method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For shadow segmentation, we additionally report Shadow-BER (S-BER) and Non-shadow-BER (N-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: BER) for class-specific assessment (Vicente et al., 2017).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Efficiency Comparisons. As illustrated in Fig. 2, SegDINO demonstrates remarkable parameter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiency while maintaining superior segmentation performance across both medical and natural

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets. On Kvasir, SegDINO achieves the best performance with only 2.21M trainable param-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eters. On the VMD-D dataset, SegDINO again delivers superior performance under a similarly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compact parameter budget. Moreover, SegDINO sustains an inference speed of 53 FPS, exceeding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most transformer-based methods while being slightly lower than convolution-based architectures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These results highlight that SegDINO consistently achieves the most favorable trade-off among per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance, model size, and inference speed, establishing its advantage as a highly efficient solution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for both medical and natural image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work, we introduced SegDINO, a lightweight segmentation framework that couples a frozen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DINOv3 backbone with a minimal MLP-based decoder. Our design directly addresses the long-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standing challenge of adapting self-supervised representations to segmentation tasks without relying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on heavy decoders. By reformulating multi-level patch tokens into a unified representation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employing an extremely light prediction head, SegDINO achieves strong segmentation accuracy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while maintaining remarkable efficiency.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extensive experiments across six benchmarks, including three medical datasets (TN3K, Kvasir-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SEG, ISIC) and three natural image datasets (MSD, VMD-D, ViSha), consistently demonstrate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advantages of our approach. SegDINO surpasses existing state-of-the-art models by large margins

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on both natural and medical image tasks, highlighting the effectiveness of leveraging foundation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model features through a lightweight decoding pipeline. Notably, the results show that even a frozen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DINOv3 backbone, when paired with a carefully designed light decoder, can outperform models that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require significantly more parameters and computation. This validates our central hypothesis that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder simplicity does not necessarily compromise segmentation performance when foundation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: features are properly exploited.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite these strengths, SegDINO is not without limitations. First, by freezing the encoder, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adaptability of features to highly domain-specific distributions (e.g., rare pathological cases) may be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constrained. Second, while our results confirm the benefits of lightweight decoding, further ablation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studies are needed to better understand the contributions of individual components, such as feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selection depth, reformulation strategies, and decoder design. These analyses would provide deeper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: insights into the robustness of our framework and guide future architectural refinements.
